summary: Phase 147L.2 was authorized to independently verify, verification-only, that Phase 147L.1's repair of AESIC-001 from v1.0 to v1.1 resolves Phase 147L's two Major findings (Finding 1: stage_1_outcome_ref retrievability vs. Stage 1's unconditional non-persistence; Finding 2: Stage 2 idempotency's supersede branch vs. exclusive-create, package_id-only persistence) without altering the architecture or introducing new inconsistencies. AESIC-001 v1.1 was independently reconstructed in full (1766 lines, all 28 sections), and Phase 147L's original findings were independently re-derived from primary sources before Phase 147L.1's own repair narrative was consulted for comparison. Finding 1 is confirmed resolved: AESIC-REQ-118 redefines stage_1_outcome_ref as an inline, verbatim, embedded copy written into the AER's own document body, making both-outcomes-retrievable true by construction; independently stress-tested against a malformed-embedded-record attack (caught by the AER's own digest, no separate mechanism needed). Finding 2 is confirmed resolved: the AESIC-REQ-119/120/121 two-tier compound-(package_id, evaluation_id)-keyed storage model with a package_id-keyed canonical pointer makes supersession mechanically achievable without violating immutability; independently stress-tested against constructed concurrent-attempt, duplicate-publication, and historical-replay races with no surviving ambiguity. This verification's own independent adversarial process surfaced two new, Non-Blocking findings not identified by Phase 147L or Phase 147L.1: (1) Major -- stage_1_outcome_ref's embedded content (AESIC-REQ-118) has no defined channel into evaluate_stage_2, because AES's unmodified public interface (AESIC-REQ-007/012) accepts only session/package_id, Session is explicitly forbidden (AESIC-REQ-060) from carrying Stage 1's outcome, and AES itself is stateless (AESIC-REQ-017) -- so a conforming implementation has no way to ever populate a non-absent stage_1_outcome_ref, though nothing else in the contract is affected; (2) Minor -- the new canonical pointer index (AESIC-REQ-119 item 2) has no defined tamper-evidence mechanism unlike the AER itself (AESIC-REQ-055/083). Cross-contract compatibility with AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, and CHGR-001 independently reconfirmed unaffected (zero amendments required). Every architectural invariant named in this phase's own governing prompt (AES/Registry/Decision-Template ownership, evaluator purity, disclosure-only semantics, replay/persistence/AER/lifecycle architecture, Stage 2 supersession, non-gating guarantees) independently reconfirmed preserved. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.1 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Full detail in docs/verification/PHASE_147L2_AESIC_REPAIR_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147l2_adversarial_analysis
validation_results.result: Constructed fresh adversarial scenarios (restart after Stage 1, Stage 2 without Stage 1 replay, duplicated/concurrent publication, historical replay, missing/malformed embedded record for Target 1; supersession/idempotency/replay/duplicate-execution/immutable-history/current-effective-outcome/concurrent-publication/stale-replay for Target 2; plus digest-ownership, cross-session-leakage, and record-immutability attacks) not reusing Phase 147L's own attack wording. Surfaced two new findings: (1) Major -- stage_1_outcome_ref's embedded content has no defined input channel into evaluate_stage_2 given AESIC-REQ-007/012/060/017's unmodified closure; (2) Minor -- the canonical pointer index (AESIC-REQ-119 item 2) has no defined tamper-evidence mechanism. Six additional attack paths attempted and found unsuccessful, recorded for completeness.

validation_results.name: phase_147l2_requirement_matrix
validation_results.result: Classified AESIC-REQ-118, 119, 120, and 121 individually against necessary/sufficient/internally-consistent/externally-compatible/implementable criteria; AESIC-REQ-118 found necessary but not sufficient (and not implementable as specified, pending the section 3.1 finding's future repair); AESIC-REQ-119/120/121 found necessary, sufficient (120 with the narrower section 3.2 integrity gap noted), internally consistent, externally compatible, and implementable. Contradiction-construction attempts among AESIC-REQ-118-121 themselves found none; the one genuine contradiction found is external, between AESIC-REQ-118 and the unmodified AESIC-REQ-007/012/060/017.
